source_refs.note: Topic 20.4.2, printed page 67; the examples are redrawn. The claim that the KMnO4 test distinguishes primary, secondary and tertiary alkylbenzenes is marked: primary and secondary both react.

blocks.text: Oxidation reaction that takes place at an alkyl group directly attached to a benzene ring is termed as side-chain oxidation. In this reaction, alkylbenzenes are readily oxidized by alkaline KMnO₄ or acidic K₂Cr₂O₇ or dilute HNO₃. In these kinds of reaction, the alkyl groups are oxidized to carboxylic acid group, regardless of the size of alkyl group, keeping the benzene ring intact.

blocks.alt: Toluene + 3[O], with Heat over the arrow, gives benzoic acid (the ring carrying COOH) + H2O.
blocks.caption: Side-chain oxidation of toluene (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 70).

blocks.text: Side-chain oxidation of alkylbenzene takes place when there is at least one benzylic hydrogen attached to the carbon. No reaction occurs in the absence of benzylic hydrogen. Thus, these reactions have no effect on tertiary carbons attached to an aromatic ring.

Whatever the length of an alkyl group may be, it gives only on carboxyl group as a product after oxidation. Following example demonstrates the utilization of oxidation reaction in the production of substituted benzoic acid.

blocks.alt: Three reactions with KMnO4 over and H+ under the arrow: a benzene ring carrying CH2-R gives the ring carrying C(=O)OH; tetralin, a benzene ring fused to a saturated six-membered ring, gives a benzene ring with two C(=O)OH groups on neighbouring carbons; a benzene ring carrying CR3 gives No Reaction.
blocks.caption: Side-chain oxidation with KMnO4 (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 70).

blocks.text: Both alkane and benzene are very stable and insusceptible to oxidation but when put together, the benzylic carbon which is directly attached to the benzene ring becomes more reactive and more susceptible to oxidation.

Oxidation of alkylbenzene containing benzylic protons by KMnO₄ is used an identification test. Purple colour of KMnO₄ solution is discharged, once consumed in the oxidation reaction. Therefore, one can easily differentiate between benzene, benzene containing primary, secondary, and tertiary alkyl groups by chemical test with KMnO₄ solution.
book_errors: benzene containing primary, secondary, and tertiary alkyl groups

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The KMnO₄ test cannot tell primary from secondary alkyl groups: both have benzylic hydrogen and both discharge the purple colour. It distinguishes benzene and alkylbenzenes with a tertiary alkyl group (colour stays) from those with a primary or secondary alkyl group (colour discharged).
